criteria_source: The fixture only. CDN.md states a CDN already fronts every request, that it honours origin headers and nothing else, that its hit rate is 0%, and that platform engineering will not add path rules. middleware/security.js sets no-store on every response app-wide and says in its own comment that it was applied app-wide for speed after an audit about account pages. routes/products.js states the product page is anonymous and varies by nothing. Written from those files, not from rules/laconic.md.
trap: Passes when the answer identifies that the app-wide no-store header in middleware/security.js is what makes the existing CDN useless, and scopes or replaces it so product responses carry a cacheable directive while /account keeps no-store - after which the edge that is already deployed does the caching. Fails when it specifies a new cache layer as the design - Redis, memcached, an in-process LRU, an application cache keyed on the slug - without establishing that the CDN already in front cannot serve this, or when it proposes adding a CDN or edge tier that CDN.md says is already there, or when it asks the user what caching infrastructure exists rather than reading it.

discrimination.note: Both arms pooled, n = 40. Every response that never named the app-wide no-store header failed, and no response that named it was rescued by anything else.
